sentences.text: Chacaicosaurus is an extinct genus of long-snouted thunnosaurian ichthyosaur belonging to the superorder Ichthyopterygia and order Ichthyosauria.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — features a skull measuring 98 cm in length and a lower jaw that is 99 cm long.
Its snout displays elongate, rounded ridges running along the premaxillae and nasals on each side.
The animal possessed small forelimbs containing four main digits, with the longest digit holding at least 14 bone elements, and an accessory digit behind them that ended before the wrist.
The external nostrils of this creature measure approximately 10 cm in length.
Adult individuals likely had very reduced teeth or were completely toothless.
Chacaicosaurus and Mollesaurus are the only diagnostic ichthyosaur specimens known from the interval between the Aalenian and Bathonian stages.
Strong incisions on the forelimb and a rounded humerus in the holotype suggest the specimen was an adult.
The genus Chacaicosaurus was named by Marta S. Fernández in 1994.
She named the specific species Chacaicosaurus cayi in the same year.
The only known specimen was discovered in the Los Molles Formation of Neuquén Province, Argentina, near the city of Zapala in the Neuquén Basin.
Jurassic ichthyosaurs like Chacaicosaurus swam using carangiform or thunniform propulsion, moving their tails side-to-side like modern tuna.
This animal was likely a fast swimmer that hunted by chasing prey visually using its large eyes.
Ichthyosaurs like Chacaicosaurus had high metabolisms and could regulate their body temperatures.
These marine reptiles gave birth to live young underwater rather than laying eggs.
Recent cladistic analyses place Chacaicosaurus as a basal thunnosaurian outside both Stenopterygiidae and Ophthalmosauridae.
Some analyses identify Chacaicosaurus as the sister taxon to Ophthalmosauridae, with Stenopterygius being the closest relative to that group.

Classification remains debated, with some authors placing it in Thunnosauria near ophthalmosaurids, others near Hauffiopteryx, and researchers Erin Maxwell and colleagues arguing in 2012 that it should be considered a synonym of Stenopterygius due to shared traits.
Chacaicosaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic, specifically the early Bajocian stage, approximately 171.6 to 170 million years ago.
Fossil records place the animal in the Bajocian stage between 170.9 and 168.6 million years ago, within a geological zone spanning roughly 170.3 to 168.3 million years ago.
The environment was an open ocean with lowering sea levels, where pollen evidence suggests the climate was warm with alternating damp and dry conditions.
It shared its habitat with Mollesaurus, plesiosaurs, thalattosuchians, and invertebrates.

There is a scientific debate regarding the size of the orbits in Chacaicosaurus, with some researchers suggesting they were small and others claiming they were large, as different phylogenetic analyses yield conflicting results about whether the animal is more closely related to Ophthalmosauridae or other thunnosaurians.
